# Virling

> Virling is open-source revenue attribution for B2B SaaS, online stores and agencies, self-hosted or hosted. It joins every website visit to the payment that followed, so marketing teams, store owners, agencies and founders can see which traffic channel brings paying customers, not just visitors. It reads payments from Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy, Creem and RevenueCat, and links LemonSqueezy payments to visits through a webhook when Virling has an https address. It runs as one Rust binary under the AGPLv3 license.

Virling answers questions like: which channel brought the most revenue this month, did a launch or a Reddit post make money or just traffic, what is a visitor from each source worth, and which visits did a paying customer have before they paid.

Releases are on GitHub and can be self-hosted today. Hosted plans start with a 14-day free trial at https://app.virling.com/login: Personal $19 a month and Agency $79 a month, with the first 50 customers of each plan paying $9 and $29 for life.

Every page on virling.com also has a Markdown copy at its address plus .md, such as https://virling.com/pricing.md, and https://virling.com/index.md for the home page.

## Product

- [Home](https://virling.com/): what Virling does, how attribution works, and the self-host spec
- [Pricing](https://virling.com/pricing): free to self-host; hosted Personal $19 and Agency $79 a month after a 14-day free trial, founding price $9 and $29 for the first 50 customers of each plan
- [Self-host](https://virling.com/self-host): one Rust binary with embedded storage for Linux, macOS or Docker, free under AGPLv3
- [For agencies](https://virling.com/agency): weekly branded reports that show each client which channels brought paying customers
- [Integrations](https://virling.com/integrations): one page per payment provider, for Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy, Creem and RevenueCat
- [Live demo](https://virling.com/demo/): a static demo dashboard with made-up data
- [Free tools](https://virling.com/tools): browser tools with no signup
- [UTM builder](https://virling.com/tools/utm-builder): add utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign to any link
- [Revenue per visitor and ROI calculator](https://virling.com/tools/revenue-per-visitor): revenue per visitor, return on ad spend and break-even per channel
- [Stripe fee calculator](https://virling.com/tools/payment-fee-calculator): what Stripe charges per sale, compared with Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Polar, Dodo Payments and Creem on your own price
- [AI crawler checker](https://virling.com/tools/ai-crawler-checker): see which AI crawlers a robots.txt allows or blocks
- [CAC payback calculator](https://virling.com/tools/cac-payback-calculator): months to earn back acquisition cost from monthly revenue per customer and gross margin
- [Checkout snippet generator](https://virling.com/tools/checkout-snippet-generator): pick a payment provider and copy the code that passes the visitor ID into checkout
- [LTV to CAC ratio calculator](https://virling.com/tools/ltv-cac-calculator): lifetime value, acquisition cost, LTV to CAC ratio and payback months per channel
- [Average order value calculator](https://virling.com/tools/aov-calculator): average order value overall and per channel for ecommerce stores
- [Attribution model calculator](https://virling.com/tools/attribution-model-calculator): how five attribution models split one payment across a journey of 2 to 6 channels
- [Customer acquisition cost calculator](https://virling.com/tools/cac-calculator): blended and per-channel customer acquisition cost, including shared costs
- [Churn rate calculator](https://virling.com/tools/churn-rate-calculator): customer churn, revenue churn and implied average customer lifetime
- [Conversion rate calculator by channel](https://virling.com/tools/conversion-rate-calculator): conversion rate, revenue per visitor and average order value per channel
- [MRR calculator](https://virling.com/tools/mrr-calculator): MRR, ARR and net new MRR from plans and new, expansion, contraction and churned MRR
- [ROAS calculator](https://virling.com/tools/roas-calculator): return on ad spend, break-even ROAS and profit or loss from spend, revenue and gross margin
- [UTM checker](https://virling.com/tools/utm-checker): find missing source or medium, capitals, spaces, duplicate parameters and other mistakes in tagged links
- [UTM naming convention template](https://virling.com/tools/utm-naming-template): source, medium and campaign naming for email, social, paid ads, partners and podcasts, copy as CSV
- [Client marketing report template](https://virling.com/tools/agency-client-report-template): monthly report for agency clients with revenue and paying customers by channel, change versus last month, top campaigns and next steps, copy as CSV
- [Marketing budget allocation calculator](https://virling.com/tools/marketing-budget-calculator): ROAS, share of spend versus share of revenue and a suggested split of next month's budget from spend and revenue per channel
- [Net revenue retention calculator](https://virling.com/tools/nrr-calculator): net and gross revenue retention from starting MRR, expansion, contraction and churned MRR
- [Shopify fee calculator](https://virling.com/tools/shopify-fee-calculator): what Shopify takes per order and per month on each plan, with Shopify Payments or a third-party gateway
- [Traffic source checker](https://virling.com/tools/traffic-source-checker): paste a landing URL and referrer to see which channel Virling credits, the rule that matched and the tagging mistakes behind it
- [Repeat purchase rate calculator](https://virling.com/tools/repeat-purchase-rate-calculator): repeat purchase rate, purchase frequency and average days between orders, overall and per first channel, for ecommerce stores
- [ARPU calculator](https://virling.com/tools/arpu-calculator): average revenue per user and per account, monthly and annual, from MRR or ARR, paying accounts and users
- [Break-even CPA calculator](https://virling.com/tools/break-even-cpa-calculator): the most you can pay per customer and a target CPA from order value or monthly price, gross margin and orders or months per customer
- [Questions to ask an AI assistant about revenue by channel](https://virling.com/tools/ai-revenue-questions): 26 questions to ask Claude, ChatGPT or another AI assistant about revenue by channel once Virling's MCP server is connected
- [Marketing channel scorecard template](https://virling.com/tools/channel-scorecard-template): visitors, signups, paying customers, revenue, revenue per visitor, spend and CAC per channel with a keep, test or cut rule, copy as CSV
- [LTV calculator](https://virling.com/tools/ltv-calculator): customer lifetime value from ARPU, gross margin and churn, or from order value, purchases per year and years retained, with an optional table per channel
- [Marketing ROI calculator](https://virling.com/tools/marketing-roi-calculator): ROI and profit from spend, revenue and gross margin for up to 8 channels, and which channels pay back best
- [Email subscriber value calculator](https://virling.com/tools/email-subscriber-value-calculator): revenue per subscriber per month and per year, and what a new subscriber is worth, from list size, sends, click rate, conversion rate and order value
- [SaaS quick ratio calculator](https://virling.com/tools/quick-ratio-calculator): the SaaS quick ratio from new, expansion, contraction and churned MRR, plus new MRR by channel
- [Influencer ROI calculator](https://virling.com/tools/influencer-roi-calculator): ROI, revenue per post and break-even conversion rate from the creator fee, product cost, clicks, conversion rate and order value
- [Affiliate commission calculator](https://virling.com/tools/affiliate-commission-calculator): payout per sale and over a customer's lifetime, one-time or recurring, and the highest commission rate that still breaks even
- [Lead value calculator](https://virling.com/tools/lead-value-calculator): what a B2B SaaS lead is worth and the most you can pay per lead, from leads per month, lead to paid rate and first-year revenue per customer
- [Product launch tracking checklist](https://virling.com/tools/launch-tracking-checklist): UTM tags and short links before a launch, what to log on launch day, and revenue and renewals by channel 30 days after. Print it or copy it as Markdown
- [Customer retention rate calculator](https://virling.com/tools/customer-retention-rate-calculator): customer retention rate from customers at the start and end of a period and the new customers gained, with the formula shown
- [Trial to paid conversion rate calculator](https://virling.com/tools/trial-to-paid-calculator): free trial to paid conversion rate from trials started and trials that paid, overall or per acquisition channel
- [How did you hear about us survey template](https://virling.com/tools/how-did-you-hear-about-us-template): answer options for SaaS and stores, where to ask the question, and how to compare the answers with tracked sources
- [MER calculator](https://virling.com/tools/mer-calculator): marketing efficiency ratio, break-even MER and profit after marketing from total revenue, total marketing cost and gross margin
- [Contribution margin per order calculator](https://virling.com/tools/contribution-margin-calculator): contribution margin per order for ecommerce stores, after product cost, shipping, payment fees and acquisition cost
- [A/B test calculator with revenue per visitor](https://virling.com/tools/ab-test-calculator): conversion rate, lift, two-sided z-test significance and revenue per visitor for two variants
- [Cart abandonment rate calculator: carts, orders and lost revenue](https://virling.com/tools/cart-abandonment-rate-calculator): Free cart abandonment rate calculator for ecommerce stores. Enter carts created and orders completed to see your abandonment rate and the revenue left in carts. Runs in your browser.
- [Annual plan discount calculator: monthly vs annual pricing](https://virling.com/tools/annual-discount-calculator): annual price, effective monthly price and break-even customer lifetime from your monthly price, discount and churn
- [Revenue growth rate calculator: MoM, CMGR and annual growth](https://virling.com/tools/revenue-growth-rate-calculator): total growth, compound monthly growth rate (CMGR) and annualized growth from starting and ending revenue
- [SaaS magic number calculator: sales efficiency from revenue growth](https://virling.com/tools/saas-magic-number-calculator): how much new annual revenue each dollar of last quarter's sales and marketing spend bought
- [Burn multiple calculator: cash burned per dollar of new ARR](https://virling.com/tools/burn-multiple-calculator): Free burn multiple calculator. Enter net burn and net new ARR for the same period to see how much cash you burn to add each dollar of annual recurring revenue. Runs in your browser.
- [Rule of 40 calculator: SaaS growth plus profit margin](https://virling.com/tools/rule-of-40-calculator): Free Rule of 40 calculator for SaaS. Enter your revenue growth rate and your EBITDA or free cash flow margin to see your Rule of 40 score and how far it is from 40. Runs in your browser.
- [Investor update template: monthly update with revenue by channel](https://virling.com/tools/investor-update-template): Free investor update template for founders: highlights, key metrics, revenue by acquisition channel, what worked, what did not and asks. Fill it in your browser and copy it as Markdown or plain text for a monthly email.

## Integrations

- [Stripe](https://virling.com/integrations/stripe): read-only restricted key
- [Paddle](https://virling.com/integrations/paddle): Paddle Billing, read-only API key
- [Shopify](https://virling.com/integrations/shopify): read-only order token and a theme snippet
- [WooCommerce](https://virling.com/integrations/woocommerce): read-only REST API key, works with WooCommerce Subscriptions
- [Dodo Payments](https://virling.com/integrations/dodo-payments): API key, payment links need no code
- [Polar](https://virling.com/integrations/polar): read-only organization token
- [LemonSqueezy](https://virling.com/integrations/lemonsqueezy): API key and a signed webhook
- [Creem](https://virling.com/integrations/creem): scoped API key and a signed webhook
- [RevenueCat](https://virling.com/integrations/revenuecat): web purchases and renewals by webhook, credited when they carry a visitor ID
- [Revenue attribution for SaaS](https://virling.com/integrations/saas): trials, renewals, retention and MRR by first source
- [Revenue attribution for ecommerce](https://virling.com/integrations/ecommerce): orders and revenue by channel for Shopify and WooCommerce stores, and which first source brings repeat buyers
- [Revenue attribution for digital products](https://virling.com/integrations/digital-products): sales of templates, courses, ebooks and small software by channel, for LemonSqueezy, Polar, Creem and Dodo Payments

- [Why GA4 revenue doesn't match Stripe or Shopify](https://virling.com/blog/ga4-revenue-does-not-match-stripe): eight reasons GA4 and your payment provider disagree on revenue, how to check each one, and which number to trust.
- [Why Shopify orders show up as Direct, and how to fix it](https://virling.com/blog/shopify-orders-show-as-direct): untagged emails, in-app browsers, other domains and long buying cycles push Shopify orders into Direct.
- [Why is Direct your biggest traffic source? What it hides](https://virling.com/blog/why-is-direct-my-biggest-traffic-source): Direct is what is left when a visit has no referrer, UTM tag or known app; how to shrink it and credit sales with last non-direct.
- [Best revenue analytics tools in 2026, by what they answer](https://virling.com/blog/best-revenue-analytics-tools): Revenue analytics means three different things. Twelve tools for channel revenue, subscription metrics and web analytics, with prices checked from each vendor's site.
- [Find which marketing channel pays](https://virling.com/blog/find-which-channel-pays): five steps to measure revenue per visitor by channel

- [How to see how much revenue Reddit brings you](https://virling.com/blog/how-much-revenue-does-reddit-bring): Tag links per subreddit, handle visits from the Reddit app that arrive with no referrer, and compare Reddit's revenue per visitor with your average.
- [Revenue per visitor: formula, average and how to calculate](https://virling.com/blog/what-is-revenue-per-visitor): Revenue per visitor (RPV) is revenue divided by unique visitors. How to calculate it, what a good average is, why it matters and how to raise it.
- [First-touch or last-touch attribution for a SaaS](https://virling.com/blog/first-touch-vs-last-touch-attribution-saas): First touch credits the visit that found you. Last touch credits the visit before the payment. Which to use for a small SaaS, with an example.
- [How to track Stripe revenue by traffic source](https://virling.com/blog/track-stripe-revenue-by-traffic-source): Stripe knows who paid, not where they came from. Pass the visitor ID into checkout so each payment can be joined to the visit before it.
- [Which UTM parameters to use to trace revenue](https://virling.com/blog/utm-parameters-for-revenue-tracking): Five UTM parameters, the naming rules that keep reports clean, and the mistakes that send revenue to Direct.
- [Is AI search traffic worth anything? How to measure it](https://virling.com/blog/is-ai-search-traffic-worth-anything): Visitors from ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude are few, but they can pay well. How to count them and compare their revenue per visitor.
- [How long does a visitor take to become a customer?](https://virling.com/blog/how-long-does-a-visitor-take-to-become-a-customer): Time to pay is the gap between the first visit and the first payment. How to measure it per channel and what to change when it is long.
- [Trial-to-paid conversion by traffic source, step by step](https://virling.com/blog/trial-to-paid-conversion-by-traffic-source): Track the trial start as a goal, credit the first charge to the visits before the trial, and compare each channel's trial-to-paid rate.
- [How to track Paddle revenue by traffic source](https://virling.com/blog/track-paddle-revenue-by-traffic-source): Paddle knows who paid, not where they came from. Pass the visitor ID in custom data at checkout so each transaction can be joined to the visit before it.

- [How to track Shopify revenue by traffic source](https://virling.com/blog/track-shopify-revenue-by-traffic-source): Shopify knows who ordered, not where they came from. Store a visitor ID on the cart so each order carries it, then join orders to the visits before them.
- [Cross-domain checkout: keep the source of every sale](https://virling.com/blog/cross-domain-checkout-attribution): Buyers who leave for checkout.stripe.com or another domain lose your analytics cookie. How to keep the traffic source of each sale, case by case.

- [How to track WooCommerce revenue by traffic source](https://virling.com/blog/track-woocommerce-revenue-by-traffic-source): WooCommerce knows who ordered, not which channel sent them. Save a visitor ID on each order so it can be joined to the visits before it.
- [LinkedIn revenue tracking for B2B SaaS](https://virling.com/blog/linkedin-revenue-tracking): Is LinkedIn worth it for your SaaS? Tag posts and profile links, handle the in-app browser, and see the revenue and revenue per visitor LinkedIn brings.

- [Dark social traffic: what it is and what revenue it brings](https://virling.com/blog/dark-social-revenue-tracking): Dark social traffic is links shared in chats, DMs and email that arrive with no referrer. Where it comes from, how to spot it, and how to see its revenue.
- [Attribution window: how long a visit gets credit](https://virling.com/blog/attribution-window): An attribution window is how many days before a payment a visit can earn credit. How its length changes which channel gets credit, and how to pick one.

- [Guest post revenue tracking: which articles bring paying customers](https://virling.com/blog/guest-post-revenue-tracking): How to track revenue from guest posts, roundups and press mentions: how referrals are credited, how to ask for tagged links, and how to compare articles by paying customers over 90 days.
- [Paddle UTM tracking: pass UTM and custom data to checkout](https://virling.com/blog/paddle-checkout-utm-parameters): How to tie a Paddle transaction to the visit and channel that brought it: where UTM tags get lost on overlay and hosted checkout, and how to pass custom data.
- [LemonSqueezy UTM tracking: which channel brought each order](https://virling.com/blog/lemonsqueezy-utm-tracking): How to see which channel brought each LemonSqueezy order: pass a visitor ID as checkout custom data, from a checkout link, the browser or checkout_data.custom on your server.
- [Perplexity referral traffic: which Perplexity visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/perplexity-revenue-tracking): How to track traffic from Perplexity and its revenue: the perplexity.ai referrer, utm_source tags, app visits that look direct, and how the payment is credited.
- [How to track sponsorship ROI: newsletters, podcasts and YouTube](https://virling.com/blog/sponsorship-revenue-tracking): Track the revenue each paid sponsorship brought: a UTM per sponsor, tracked short links for spoken or printed URLs, and the placement fee next to attributed revenue.
- [Referral program tracking: see the revenue referred customers bring](https://virling.com/blog/referral-program-revenue-tracking): How to track customer referrals by revenue: one tagged link or tracked short link per referrer, the payment it shows on, and renewals that stay credited to the referral.
- [Gemini referral traffic: which Gemini visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/gemini-revenue-tracking): How to track traffic from Gemini and the revenue it brings: the gemini.google.com referrer, utm_source tags, app visits that look direct, and how the payment is credited.
- [Bluesky traffic analytics: track sales from Bluesky posts](https://virling.com/blog/bluesky-revenue-tracking): How to see which Bluesky posts bring paying customers: bsky.app referrers, UTM-tagged links, apps that send no referrer, and visits joined to payments.
- [Track signups from dev.to and Medium: which articles bring paying customers](https://virling.com/blog/dev-to-medium-revenue-tracking): How to see which dev.to and Medium articles bring paying customers: how their visits are classified, how to tag the links in each article, and what canonical and cross-posting change.
- [Microsoft Copilot traffic: which Copilot visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/copilot-revenue-tracking): How to track Microsoft Copilot traffic and the revenue it brings: the copilot.microsoft.com referrer, how it differs from Bing search, and how the payment is credited.
- [WhatsApp revenue tracking for stores and SaaS](https://virling.com/blog/whatsapp-revenue-tracking): Why WhatsApp clicks land as Direct, how to tag broadcast, status and click-to-chat links, and how to credit Shopify, WooCommerce or Stripe revenue to WhatsApp.
- [Discount code attribution: what codes miss and how to cross-check them](https://virling.com/blog/discount-code-attribution): Discount code attribution explained: what coupon codes can and cannot tell you, how codes leak, and how to use tracked links and codes together as a cross-check.
- [Polar UTM tracking: which channel brought each order](https://virling.com/blog/polar-utm-tracking): How to see which channel brought each Polar order: checkout links on buy.polar.sh get a reference_id with no code, and checkout sessions take virling_vid in metadata.
- [Claude revenue tracking: which Claude visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/claude-revenue-tracking): How to track traffic from Claude and the revenue it brings: the claude.ai referrer, utm_source tags, visits that count as Direct, and how payments are credited.
- [Indie Hackers revenue tracking: which posts and milestones bring paying customers](https://virling.com/blog/indie-hackers-revenue-tracking): Indie Hackers revenue tracking for SaaS founders: how posts, milestones, product pages and comments show up as referrers, when to add UTM tags, and which post paid.
- [Threads revenue tracking: which Threads posts bring paying customers](https://virling.com/blog/threads-revenue-tracking): How to track sales from Threads: threads.com and l.threads.com referrers, profile and post links, in-app browser clicks, and comparing Threads with Instagram.
- [Dodo Payments UTM tracking: pass source data through checkout](https://virling.com/blog/dodo-payments-utm-tracking): How to tie a Dodo Payments payment to the visit and channel that brought it: payment links, checkout sessions and links built in code.
- [RevenueCat web paywall attribution: which channel brought each subscriber](https://virling.com/blog/revenuecat-web-paywall-attribution): RevenueCat web paywall attribution means tying each web purchase to the visit before it. Store the visitor ID on the customer, and know what stays Unattributed.
- [How to prove marketing ROI to clients: a monthly method for agencies](https://virling.com/blog/prove-marketing-roi-to-clients): How to prove marketing ROI to clients: tag every link, connect the client's payment provider, report revenue by channel monthly and explain Unattributed.
- [WooCommerce UTM tracking: where UTMs show on orders](https://virling.com/blog/woocommerce-utm-tracking): Where WooCommerce stores UTM parameters on an order, why they go missing, and how to see revenue per UTM campaign for your store.
- [Quora revenue tracking: which answers bring paying customers](https://virling.com/blog/quora-revenue-tracking): Quora revenue tracking for SaaS and online stores: tag links in answers, Spaces and your profile, and see which answers bring paying customers, not just views.
- [ChatGPT revenue tracking: which ChatGPT visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/chatgpt-revenue-tracking): How to track ChatGPT traffic and revenue: the chatgpt.com referrer, the utm_source=chatgpt.com tag, visits with no referrer, and how the payment is credited.
- [Build in public with a revenue dashboard: share revenue by channel](https://virling.com/blog/public-revenue-dashboard): How to share revenue publicly with Virling: a read-only dashboard of revenue by channel at /share/yourdomain.com, with a switch to hide the dollar amounts.
- [Stripe Payment Link UTM tracking: see which source sold](https://virling.com/blog/stripe-payment-links-utm-tracking): Stripe Payment Links drop your UTM tags and the referrer. See what a Payment Link keeps, and how to track the source of every Payment Link sale with no code.
- [Creem UTM tracking: which channel brought each payment](https://virling.com/blog/creem-utm-tracking): How to see which channel brought each Creem payment: create the checkout on your server with virling_vid in metadata, and Virling reads it from the webhook.
- [DeepSeek referral traffic: which DeepSeek visits pay](https://virling.com/blog/deepseek-revenue-tracking): How to track DeepSeek referral traffic and revenue: the chat.deepseek.com referrer, utm_source tags, visits with no referrer, and how the payment is credited.
- [Multi-touch attribution for a small business](https://virling.com/blog/multi-touch-attribution): Multi-touch attribution splits credit for a sale across several visits. Linear and position-based explained with an example, and when a small team needs it.
- [UTM parameters lost after redirect: causes and fixes](https://virling.com/blog/utm-parameters-lost-after-redirect): UTM tags usually vanish in a server redirect that drops the query string. How to test each redirect with curl, and fixes for Nginx, Caddy, SPAs and checkout.
- [MRR by acquisition channel: which channels bring MRR](https://virling.com/blog/mrr-by-acquisition-channel): How to see new MRR, churned MRR and renewals per acquisition channel: credit each subscription to the channel that brought the customer, then read retention per channel.
- [iOS Link Tracking Protection: does Safari remove UTM parameters?](https://virling.com/blog/ios-link-tracking-protection-utm): What Apple documents about Link Tracking Protection in Mail, Messages and Safari Private Browsing, what it says about UTM tags, and how to keep revenue attribution.
- [Framer analytics revenue: track Stripe payment link sales](https://virling.com/blog/framer-revenue-tracking): See which channel brought each sale from a Framer site. Add one script in Framer custom code, keep plain Stripe, Polar, Dodo or LemonSqueezy checkout links, and connect the provider.
- [Grok referral traffic: how to track traffic from Grok](https://virling.com/blog/grok-revenue-tracking): How to track traffic from Grok and see which Grok visits pay: the grok.com referrer in the Referral channel, utm tags on your links, and how the payment is credited.
- [Webflow analytics revenue: track Stripe sales by channel](https://virling.com/blog/webflow-revenue-tracking): See which channel brought each sale from your Webflow site. Add one script in Webflow site settings, keep your Stripe checkout links, and track every sale by source.
- [Next.js Stripe Checkout UTM tracking: pass the visit to the session](https://virling.com/blog/nextjs-stripe-utm-tracking): How to tie a Stripe Checkout payment in a Next.js App Router app to the visit and UTM tags that brought it, with a route handler and a server action.
- [Carrd revenue tracking: see which channel brings each sale](https://virling.com/blog/carrd-revenue-tracking): Carrd revenue tracking for one-page sites: add the script with an embed element, keep plain Stripe Payment Links or LemonSqueezy checkout links, connect the provider, and see which channel brought each sale.
- [Track Stripe revenue by traffic source in an AI-built app](https://virling.com/blog/vibe-coded-app-revenue-tracking): Built your app with Lovable, Bolt, Replit or Cursor and added Stripe? One prompt adds the Virling script and passes the visitor ID to Checkout, so each payment shows its channel.
